note: Platform blueprints carried from the earlier 20-problem build (B2B Services). Fixed input for scripts/build-dataset.js.

entries.title: Why can't SMEs negotiate favorable payment terms with large buyers?
entries.pitch: Payment-term infrastructure that gives an SME supplier the leverage of a large buyer.
entries.who: SME suppliers selling to large corporates on 60–120 day payment cycles.
how: Benchmark payment terms by buyer and industry so a supplier knows what is normal before signing.
Offer buyer-backed reverse factoring: underwrite the receivable, not the SME, and settle in days for a small discount.
Automate e-invoicing, collection nudges and a dispute desk so cash does not stall on paperwork.
mvp: Two NBFC partners and 20 buyer programmes
entries.model: Factoring spread, supplier SaaS, benchmark subscription for larger suppliers.
entries.price: 0.5–1.5% per invoice financed. ₹4,999/month for the platform.
entries.gtm: Industry clusters such as auto components and textiles, CA networks and large-buyer supplier programmes.
entries.moat: Receivable performance data by buyer plus capital partnerships. Hard to bootstrap, valuable once live.

market.tam: ₹50 lakh Cr+ in B2B receivables, with MSME working capital as the wedge

entries.verdict: This is the highest-itch problem on the platform for a reason: cash flow is the SME's real product.

entries.title: Why can’t manufacturers rely on guaranteed, accountable pickup logistics for outbound deliveries?
entries.pitch: SLA-backed first-mile pickup with proof, penalties and payout on delivery.
entries.who: D2C brands and manufacturers shipping outbound from two or three warehouses.
how: Book pickup slots with vetted fleets and attach a penalty-backed SLA to every slot.
Capture photo, weight and condition proof at pickup, then release payment only after confirmed delivery.
Run an exception desk for damages and delays, with insurance attached to high-value loads.
mvp: Two anchor clients on monthly SLA
entries.model: Per-pickup fee plus an SLA subscription, insurance commission.
entries.gtm: D2C clusters in NCR and Bengaluru, plus 3PL partnerships that lack first-mile reliability.
entries.moat: Reliability data and driver density. Operations discipline is the barrier.
risks: Capex if the fleet is owned

market.tam: ₹20,000 Cr+ first-mile logistics spend, growing with D2C

entries.verdict: Brands sell a delivery promise. First-mile is where that promise quietly breaks.

entries.title: Why do factory owners wait days for industrial repair technicians?
entries.pitch: Industrial repair in hours, with vetted technicians and remote diagnostics first.
entries.who: Factory owners and plant managers with a production line down.
how: Verify technicians by machine type and skill, with a live availability calendar across industrial clusters.
Run remote video triage before dispatch, so the right technician and part arrive together.
Price on an SLA and share a downtime calculator that makes the cost of waiting explicit.
mvp: Spare-part partners for top 20 failure modes
entries.model: Commission on jobs, annual maintenance contracts, parts margin.
entries.gtm: Industrial associations, machine OEMs and plant WhatsApp groups.
entries.moat: Technician density and repair history by machine model. The data makes dispatch smarter.

market.tam: ₹25,000 Cr+ industrial maintenance and repair spend

entries.verdict: A day of downtime can cost more than a year of the repair contract. Price the urgency, not the hour.

entries.title: Why can't businesses verify new suppliers before purchasing?
entries.pitch: A trust score for new suppliers, built from registries, audits and live delivery data.
entries.who: Procurement teams at mid-market manufacturers and D2C brands onboarding new suppliers.
how: Pull GST, ROC, litigation and credit signals into one report with a plain-language risk score.
Add a quality audit from a vetted inspector and verified references from actual buyers.
Monitor the supplier continuously and alert the buyer when filings, ownership or delivery performance change.
entries.model: Per-report fee, annual monitoring subscription, audit fees.
entries.gtm: Procurement consultants, industry bodies and B2B marketplaces that need a trust layer.
entries.moat: Supplier graph and audit history. Every report improves the next one.

market.tam: ₹5 lakh Cr+ in annual B2B procurement, with supplier onboarding as the entry point

entries.verdict: Buyers already pay for due diligence with time and bad debt. Sell it as a report they can defend.

entries.title: Why do freelancers ghost projects after partial payments without accountability systems?
entries.pitch: Milestone escrow and dispute resolution for freelance projects, so nobody ghosts.
entries.who: Freelancers and small agencies working with clients they have never met.
how: Create milestone contracts with funded escrow before work starts, so the money exists before the deliverable.
Release funds on approval, with a structured revision window instead of endless feedback.
Provide mediation and a small-claims arbitration panel, plus portable reputation across clients.
entries.model: Escrow fee, premium contracts, arbitration fees.
entries.price: 1.5–2.5% of escrowed value. ₹299 for a custom contract.
entries.gtm: Freelancer communities, agency networks and invoicing tools that already hold the relationship.
entries.moat: Dispute data and a portable trust graph. Regulation is a barrier and a moat.

market.tam: India's 1.5 crore+ freelance workforce and its unpaid-invoice problem

entries.verdict: Both sides of a freelance deal are afraid. A neutral referee can charge both of them.

entries.title: Why do businesses struggle finding reliable contract manufacturers for small batches?
entries.pitch: Small-batch contract manufacturing, matched on capacity, quality and lead time.
entries.who: D2C brands and hardware startups needing 500–5,000 units to test a market.
how: Map factory capacity by machine, process and open slots, then expose only genuinely available small-batch windows.
Run a design-for-manufacturing check before quoting, so the buyer does not pay for an avoidable re-tool.
Hold a quality escrow: release payment after sample approval and a third-party inspection.
entries.model: Transaction fee, DFM services, inspection fees.
entries.price: 3–5% of order value. ₹5,000 per DFM review.
entries.gtm: D2C communities, accelerator cohorts and factory associations.
entries.moat: A factory-capacity graph with quality history. Supply is the hard side to build.

market.tam: ₹15,000 Cr+ small-batch contract manufacturing, driven by D2C

entries.verdict: Every D2C brand starts with a batch too small for a real factory. Be the bridge they never had.

entries.title: Why can’t small restaurants access wholesale ingredient pricing without large minimum orders?
entries.pitch: Wholesale ingredient buying for small restaurants, without the 100 kg minimum.
entries.who: Independent cafés, cloud kitchens and small restaurants buying 20–40 ingredients a week.
how: Pool orders across nearby kitchens to unlock wholesale prices without each kitchen meeting the MOQ.
Run a cold-chain last mile with transparent live pricing and next-morning delivery windows.
Add standing orders, credit terms and spoilage-aware forecasting so kitchens order less, more often.
entries.model: Product margin, delivery fee, supplier promotions.
entries.gtm: Cloud-kitchen hubs, chef communities and distributor partnerships for sourcing.
entries.moat: Pooled demand density and spoilage data. Density is everything in perishables.

market.tam: ₹40,000 Cr+ restaurant food supply, with 1 lakh+ small kitchens

entries.verdict: Small kitchens do not need cheaper food as much as they need to stop over-ordering it.

entries.title: Why are small retailers forced into distributor margins without direct brand access?
entries.pitch: Direct brand-to-retailer ordering with transparent margins and next-day replenishment.
entries.who: Neighbourhood retailers and emerging D2C brands trying to reach them.
how: Give retailers one ordering app with brand catalogues, landed prices and transparent margins.
Aggregate last-mile delivery through existing distributors instead of duplicating their trucks.
Send sell-through data back to brands so they can plan production and targeted offers.
mvp: 200 retailers and 15 brands in one city
entries.model: Take rate on orders, brand data subscriptions, credit referral.
entries.gtm: Retail associations, brand sales teams and distributor partnerships.
entries.moat: Retailer density and brand sell-through data.

market.tam: ₹80 lakh Cr+ retail distribution, with 1.2 crore kirana stores

entries.verdict: The distributor is not the enemy; the opaque margin is. Sell transparency and reliability together.

entries.title: Why can't shops see real-time supplier stock levels?
entries.pitch: Live supplier stock levels for small shops, without asking 'bhaiya, hai kya?'
entries.who: Kirana and specialty retailers ordering from 10–20 distributors.
how: Integrate with distributor POS and ERP systems to publish live availability and batch-level stock.
Let retailers order on WhatsApp with substitute suggestions when an SKU is short.
Add demand forecasting and auto-replenishment for the top 100 SKUs.
entries.model: Retailer SaaS, distributor subscription, fulfilment fee.
entries.price: ₹499–999/month per retailer. Distributors pay for demand analytics.
entries.gtm: Distributor networks and retail associations in one city.
entries.moat: Distributor integrations are tedious and sticky. Build the boring pipe.

market.tam: 12 million+ retail outlets and their distributor networks

entries.verdict: A stockout is a customer lost to the shop next door. Sell certainty, not software.

entries.title: Why do micro-SMEs waste 10+ hours weekly on invoice management?
entries.pitch: Accounts payable on WhatsApp: capture invoices, reconcile GST and pay on time.
entries.who: Micro-SME owners with 1–20 employees and no dedicated finance hire.
how: Let the owner forward any invoice to a WhatsApp bot, which extracts vendor, GSTIN, amount and tax.
Validate GST details, route approvals and schedule payment against due dates.
Sync the ledger to Tally or Zoho so the CA works from clean books instead of chasing photos.
entries.model: SaaS subscription, payment float, CA partner revenue share.
entries.gtm: CA firms, GST Suvidha providers and business WhatsApp groups.
entries.moat: Workflow habit plus accountant distribution. Low technical moat, so speed matters.

market.tam: 6 crore+ MSMEs, with 1 crore+ active GST filers

entries.verdict: The best interface for a micro-SME is the one already open. Build inside WhatsApp, not beside it.
